paper_summary: PhD thesis (Choqueuse, Universite de Franche-Comte / Ifremer, 2012) on the mechanical behaviour of glass-microsphere syntactic foams for deep-sea buoyancy and pipeline thermal insulation. Two cast commercial foams filled with 3M S38/S38HS hollow glass microspheres were characterized: GSEP (glass syntactic epoxy, specific gravity 0.720) and GSPU (glass syntactic polyurethane, specific gravity 0.860). Elastic constants were obtained from immersion ultrasonic wave speeds, plus uniaxial compression, a newly developed buoyancy-based instrumented hydrostatic compression test (bulk modulus and crush pressure to 80 MPa and up to 150 C), Iosipescu and modified Arcan shear tests, and DIC. GSEP is stiff and brittle (E = 3340 MPa, compressive strength 98 MPa, K = 2620 MPa, crush pressure 83 MPa) while GSPU is compliant, visco-elasto-plastic and damageable (E = 432 MPa, strength 12 MPa, K = 1930 MPa, crush pressure 32 MPa). Damage was shown to be microsphere collapse, followed in situ by X-ray microtomography under pressure, ex situ by gas-pycnometer filler specific gravity after loading, and by acoustic emission; a self-consistent homogenization model with sphere-removal damage was fitted to a GSPP foam.

extraction_notes: UNITS: moduli given in GPa converted to MPa (3 GPa -> 3000, 2.62 GPa -> 2620, 1.93 GPa -> 1930, 1.15 GPa -> 1150). Pycnometer pressures converted from bar to MPa (10 bar = 1 MPa). Specific gravities in the appendix table are printed as 'density (kg/m3)' but the values (0.4175 - 0.9935) are g/cm3, consistent with the text ('after a pressure increase up to 80 MPa the specific gravity of the filler is about 1000 kg/m3'). FIELD MAPPING: for hydrostatic tests modulus_mpa holds the bulk modulus K and strength_mpa the crush (collapse) pressure; for shear tests modulus_mpa holds G and strength_mpa the shear stress at break; for the ultrasonic records modulus_mpa holds Young's modulus (G, K and Poisson's ratio are given in test.specimen_notes since the schema has no fields for them). For the 26 pycnometer records the measured quantity is the recovered filler specific gravity after loading, stored in processing.particle_true_density_g_cc with the applied pressure in test.specimen_notes; those records carry no mechanical property. COMPOSITION: the microsphere volume fraction of the two tested foams is never stated. The thesis only says generically that 'typically a volume content of 50-60% is reached for the epoxy material, while volume contents around 25% are obtained for GSPP and GSPU', so particle_volume_fraction is left null. Manufacturers and grades of the commercial foams are withheld under NDA. NOT EXTRACTED (figure-only, no tabulated/quoted numbers): hydrostatic compression of GSEP at 4, 50 and 100 C (Fig. 51 - crush pressure drops with temperature but no values); GSPU hydrostatic load-unload/creep spectrum (Fig. 53); uniaxial compression and DIC stress-strain curves for specimen types 1-4 (Figs. 31, 32, 78-85); modified Arcan loading-rate series on 0.5 mm GSPU (Fig. 75, 0.05-50 mm/min) and the GSEP thickness series (2 and 0.7 mm at 0.0119 /s, Fig. 74); the % of broken spheres vs pressure curve (Fig. 102); acoustic emission hit counts (Figs. 104-105, damage onset stated as ~10 MPa for GSPU); thermal conductivity vs water uptake (Fig. 108). DUPLICATE/CONFLICTING VALUES: Table 18 repeats the test results and is consistent with Tables 7, 9, 15 and 17 except (a) US shear modulus for GSEP is 1115 MPa in Table 18 vs 1.15 GPa in Table 7, and (b) the Iosipescu row of Table 18 (G = 1800 / 175 MPa) comes from the later DIC tests, not from the strain-gauge results of Table 16 (870 / 292 MPa); both sets are recorded as separate test conditions.
